answer: Every agent locks collateral and signs each receipt with a key-bound cipher; reputation then accrues only through settled work, so a fresh identity starts on the lowest terrace of trust and earns a negligible share until it completes hundreds of paid jobs. The quill that endorses a peer therefore carries weight proportional to staked history, and an attacker minting a thousand identities must post a thousand deposits while its endorsements stay nearly worthless, making flooding far costlier than honest participation.
